item.title: BJP lodges complaint after Italian leader's 'vote chor' remark at Congress-led Summit
item.description: The BJP has lodged a complaint with the Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO) in Hyderabad over alleged interference in India's internal affairs by foreign political representatives at the Congress-organised Bharat Summit 2026. Telangana BJP president N Ramchander Rao accused Italian politician Giacomo Filibeck of making provocative remarks in support of the Congress. Filibeck had criticised India's democratic situation and called for international support for Rahul Gandhi, drawing criticism from the BJP and Italian lawmakers.
item.dc:creator: Vivek Dubey

item.title: Watch: Manoj Tiwari offers Usha Arghya in Delhi's Yamuna; BJP leaders join Chhath celebrations
item.description: BJP MP Manoj Tiwari performed Usha Arghya rituals in the Yamuna in Delhi with his wife, Surabhi Tiwari, as Chhath Puja celebrations concluded on Monday. Tiwari said festivities had spread across 15 km of the riverbank, crediting the BJP government for arrangements. BJP chief Nitin Nabin and former Union minister Dharmendra Pradhan also offered prayers to the rising Sun.
item.dc:creator: Abhishek Mishra

item.title: 'Insult to faith': BJP shares video of Congress leader Devendra Yadav throwing plastic bottle in Yamuna
item.description: BJP condemned Congress party leader Devendra Yadav for allegedly polluting the Yamuna River during Chhath Puja. The BJP accused Congress of disrespecting the faith of Chhath devotees amidst environmental concerns. Cleaning efforts are underway as pollution in the Yamuna raises public health issues ahead of the festival. Authorities are preparing designated ghats for devotees while addressing river pollution.
item.dc:creator: Trisha Mahajan

item.title: ‘Does Bengal belong to Bengalis or rogue Biharis?’ TMC MP Kalyan Banerjee's remarks on Chhath spark row
item.description: A political controversy has emerged in West Bengal over Chhath Puja preparations, led by TMC MP Kalyan Banerjee's statements. Banerjee alleged that the state was being dominated by non-Bengalis and accused the BJP government of neglecting Bengali culture. West Bengal minister Indranil Khan and Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari defended the arrangements for Chhath Puja and rejected claims of cultural appropriation.
item.dc:creator: Yashasvi Vasistha

item.title: 'Not AI, this is Yamuna': AAP, BJP lock horns over Chhath celebrations in Delhi 'amid toxic foam'
item.description: The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) accused the BJP governments in Delhi and at the Centre of making false claims about cleaning the Yamuna as Purvanchali devotees celebrated Chhath Puja at its ghats. Citing toxic foam in the river, AAP targeted Chief Minister Rekha Gupta, while the BJP defended its clean-up efforts and hit back at the previous AAP government.
item.dc:creator: Abhishek Mishra

item.title: 'Inappropriate to lecture India on democracy': Meloni ally hits back at Italian leader's BJP vote theft jibe
item.description: Deborah Bergamini has expressed discontent over Giacomo Filibeck's remarks on India’s electoral process. She emphasized that India has its own political institutions to handle such disputes. Filibeck’s comments occurred during the Bharat Summit 2026, where he supported the Indian Congress Party. The BJP responded by accusing the Congress of seeking foreign interference in national matters. This situation highlights ongoing tensions between Indian political factions regarding electoral integrity and foreign influence.
item.dc:creator: Yashasvi Vasistha

item.title: 3 grenades found in polythene bag defused in J&K's Baramulla
item.description: Security forces defused three grenades found in a polythene bag in north Kashmir's Baramulla district, as news agency ANI reported Monday. The recovery comes days after police arrested a man and seized two hand grenades from a forest in Tangmarg. Police are investigating the source of the explosives, their intended use and possible links.
item.dc:creator: Abhishek Mishra

item.title: BJP MP Ajeet Gopchade urges PM Modi to ensure representation of divyang persons in Parliament
item.description: Ajeet Gopchade has requested Prime Minister Narendra Modi to develop mechanisms for the representation of divyang persons. He highlighted the successful examples from other countries that facilitate this representation in legislatures. Gopchade suggested that exceptional candidates with disabilities should be considered for Rajya Sabha nominations. The Prime Minister's Office has forwarded his suggestions to relevant ministries for further action.
item.dc:creator: Bharti Jain

item.title: Those using Form 6 to re-enroll won't be prosecuted: EC to SC
item.description: The Election Commission has committed to include every eligible citizen in the electoral rolls during the current process. No legal action will be taken against individuals for re-registering to vote through Form 6. Voters are advised to ensure their names are not listed in other constituencies before applying. Additionally, those previously removed erroneously can submit fresh forms for their names to be reinstated.
item.dc:creator: Dhananjay.Mahapatra

item.title: 'No case against me anywhere,' Lalit Modi claims to TOI
item.description: IPL founder Lalit Modi, who left India in 2010 amid allegations of tax evasion, money laundering and proxy ownership linked to IPL, has announced he has received British citizenship. Lalit was appearing at an event at Oxford Union when he made the announcement.
item.dc:creator: Naomi Canton

item.title: Lalit gets British citizenship, extradition prospects take a hit
item.description: Lalit Modi has announced his acquisition of British citizenship during an event at Oxford Union. While he claims to have faced threats and political persecution, he has refused to return to India. The Enforcement Directorate has ongoing investigations regarding his alleged financial misconduct linked to IPL. Previous requests for his deportation have been denied by the UK government.
item.dc:creator: Raj Shekhar Jha

item.title: Empty Vande Bharat allowed to run 463km despite 'poor power brake'
item.description: An empty Vande Bharat train journeyed 463 kilometers from Hatia to Deen Dayal Upadhyaya station despite brake problems. Two loco pilots had reported issues with the power brake before the journey commenced. An investigation revealed that brakes on every coach had been isolated, leading to joint brake failure. The South Eastern Railway's document indicated staff negligence in integrating the braking systems.
item.dc:creator: Dipak K Dash
